---
title: "Road to Gold"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("R/data-prep.R")

medal_team_timeline <- beach_medals |>
  mutate(
    country = factor(country, levels = rev(country_medal_totals$country)),
    year = factor(year, levels = sort(unique(year))),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", country, "</b>",
      "<br>Event: ", gender,
      "<br>Year: ", year,
      "<br>Medal: ", medal
    )
  )

country_medal_progress <- medal_timeline |>
  group_by(year, country) |>
  summarise(
    edition_medals = sum(medal_count),
    cumulative_medals = sum(cumulative_medals),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", country, "</b>",
      "<br>Olympic year: ", year,
      "<br>Team medals this edition: ", edition_medals,
      "<br>Cumulative team medals: ", cumulative_medals
    )
  )

beach_athlete_age_records <- beach_athletes |>
  filter(!is.na(age)) |>
  mutate(
    medal_status = case_when(
      is.na(medal) & year >= 2020 ~ "Not reported by source",
      is.na(medal) ~ "No medal",
      TRUE ~ as.character(medal)
    ),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", name, "</b>",
      "<br>Age: ", age, " years",
      "<br>Country/team: ", country, " (NOC: ", noc, ")",
      "<br>Olympic year: ", year,
      "<br>Event: ", gender, " beach volleyball",
      "<br>Medal status: ", medal_status
    )
  )
```

## Brazil leads the Olympic beach volleyball podium

Brazil has earned **`r brazil_medals` team medals**, three more than the United States with **`r usa_medals`**. That is the most sustained success in the Olympic beach volleyball medal table, but the podium is not limited to two countries: **`r dplyr::n_distinct(beach_medals$country)`** countries have won a medal.

Brazil reached the podium at every Games from 1996 through 2016, then returned to the top of the women's podium in Paris. The United States has more golds, while Brazil's seven silvers match the U.S. total of seven golds. More recent editions brought men's golds for Norway in Tokyo and Sweden in Paris.

## Every medal, counted once

Each mark counts one medal for a **country-team pair in one event**, not one medal for each teammate. There are **`r nrow(beach_medals)`** team medals across eight editions.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Country totals aggregate 48 beach-volleyball team medals across eight editions. Sources: olympicAthletes through 2016 and official Olympic results for 2020 and 2024."

medal_leader_data <- country_medal_type_totals |>
  left_join(country_medal_totals, by = "country") |>
  mutate(country = forcats::fct_reorder(country, total_medals))

medal_leader_chart <- ggplot(
  medal_leader_data,
  aes(
    x = medal_count,
    y = country,
    fill = medal,
    text = paste0(
      as.character(country),
      "<br>", medal, ": ", medal_count,
      "<br>Total team medals: ", total_medals
    )
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72, color = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(Gold = "#c99837", Silver = "#9caab5", Bronze = "#b87950"),
    breaks = c("Gold", "Silver", "Bronze")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Team medals by country",
    x = "Team medals",
    y = "Country",
    fill = "Medal",
    caption = paste(
      "One team medal per pair and event. Sources: olympicAthletes for 1996–2016;",
      "official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "#294655"),
    plot.caption = element_text(color = "#637780", hjust = 0)
  )

plotly::ggplotly(medal_leader_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
**Observation count:** **`r nrow(beach_medals)`** team-medal results produce **`r nrow(country_medal_type_totals)`** medal-type segments across **`r dplyr::n_distinct(beach_medals$country)`** countries. Sources: `olympicAthletes` through 2016 and official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024.
:::

Brazil leads the total, while the United States leads in golds. Hover over a bar segment for its medal count and the country's total.

## How countries' medal totals changed across editions

This interactive timeline follows each country's **cumulative team medals** from Atlanta to Paris. Hover for the medals earned in an edition and the running total; click countries in the legend to focus the comparison.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Cumulative beach-volleyball team medals by country across eight Olympic editions. Each line is a country; zero-medal editions remain at the previous cumulative total."

country_progress_chart <- plotly::plot_ly(
  country_medal_progress,
  x = ~year,
  y = ~cumulative_medals,
  color = ~country,
  split = ~country,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines+markers",
  text = ~hover_text,
  hoverinfo = "text",
  colors = grDevices::hcl.colors(
    dplyr::n_distinct(country_medal_progress$country),
    palette = "Dynamic"
  ),
  marker = list(size = 7),
  line = list(width = 2)
) |>
  plotly::layout(
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Olympic edition",
      tickmode = "array",
      tickvals = sort(unique(country_medal_progress$year))
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Cumulative team medals",
      rangemode = "tozero"
    ),
    legend = list(
      title = list(text = "Country"),
      orientation = "h",
      x = 0,
      y = -0.24
    ),
    hovermode = "closest",
    margin = list(t = 30, b = 115)
  )

country_progress_chart
```

::: {.source-note}
**Observation count:** **`r nrow(beach_medals)`** real team-medal results underlie **`r nrow(country_medal_progress)`** cumulative country-edition points (**`r dplyr::n_distinct(country_medal_progress$country)`** countries across eight editions). Zero-medal editions show the unchanged cumulative total; they are not extra medal results.
:::

Brazil's cumulative lead builds across multiple editions, while newer winners such as Norway and Sweden appear in the final years. The view separates a country's medal-winning years from its total over time.

## Where each medal was won

This timeline returns to the underlying podium results: one mark per medal-winning country-team. It shows when each country's medals came and whether they were won in the men's or women's event.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "All 48 team-medal results, shown individually by country, Games year, event, and medal. Sources: olympicAthletes through 2016 and official Olympic results for 2020 and 2024."

team_medal_timeline_chart <- ggplot(
  medal_team_timeline,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = country,
    color = medal,
    text = hover_text
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~gender, ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(Gold = "#c99837", Silver = "#9caab5", Bronze = "#b87950"),
    breaks = c("Gold", "Silver", "Bronze")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Olympic year",
    y = "Medal-winning country",
    color = "Medal"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#10384a"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(color = "#355260"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "#294655")
  )

plotly::ggplotly(team_medal_timeline_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
Sources: `olympicAthletes` through 2016 and official Olympic results for Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024. Each mark is one of the **`r scales::comma(nrow(medal_team_timeline))`** country-team medal results.
:::

The podium repeats across editions for a small group of countries, but the timeline distinguishes a one-time medal from sustained performance. Hover for the exact team, medal, year, and event.

## The athletes behind the podium

This athlete-level view shows age by Olympic edition for beach volleyball competitors. Every age-reported beach-volleyball record is included; color distinguishes the men's and women's events.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Beach volleyball athlete-event records by age, event, and Olympic year. Source: olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes."

athlete_age_chart <- ggplot(
  beach_athlete_age_records,
  aes(
    x = year,
    y = age,
    color = gender,
    text = hover_text
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.18, height = 0.15, seed = 2024),
    alpha = 0.65,
    size = 2.2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Men = "#147f91", Women = "#c99837")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(beach_athlete_age_records$year))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(5)) +
  labs(
    title = "Beach volleyball competitors span generations",
    x = "Olympic year",
    y = "Age (years)",
    color = "Event"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "#355260"),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "#10384a", face = "bold")
  )

plotly::ggplotly(athlete_age_chart, tooltip = "text")
```

::: {.source-note}
**Observation count:** **`r nrow(beach_athlete_age_records)`** athlete-event records produce **`r nrow(beach_athlete_age_records)`** points, representing **`r dplyr::n_distinct(beach_athlete_age_records$id)`** distinct source IDs. All **`r nrow(beach_athletes)`** beach-volleyball records in the source have reported ages.
:::

The median age is **`r median(beach_athlete_age_records$age)`**. A point is one person's participation in one Games and event; an athlete who returns in later editions appears again, so the points are records, not unique people.

## Methodology {#methodology}

- The source is [`olympicAthletes::olympic_athletes`](https://moderndive.github.io/olympicAthletes/), a 315,094-row, 16-column athlete-event dataset. The package describes 1896–2016 records as extending the [Olympic history dataset](https://github.com/rgriff23/Olympic_history), with later records sourced from [Olympedia](https://www.olympedia.org/).
- Beach volleyball is selected by requiring `sport == "Volleyball"` **and** a beach-volleyball match in `event`. The package's 4,792-row `volleyball_athletes` subset contains indoor and beach volleyball; it is not used as a beach-volleyball count.
- For 1996–2016, the source repeats the medal on both athletes' rows. We retain one row for each Games year, event, team identifier, and medal, then normalize team suffixes (such as `-1`) only when aggregating results by country.
- The package data used here has no beach-volleyball medal labels for 2020 or 2024. We add the six podium teams for each of those editions from the [Tokyo 2020](https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/tokyo-2020/results/volleyball/beach-volleyball) and [Paris 2024](https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/paris-2024/results/volleyball/beach-volleyball) official results pages. These are team-level rows, so no athlete-level medal duplication is introduced.
- Participation charts count athlete-event rows; medal charts count medal-winning teams. A pair therefore contributes two participation records but only one medal.
- To render the site, install R packages `olympicAthletes`, `tidyverse`, `ggplot2`, `plotly`, `crosstalk`, `leaflet`, `rnaturalearth`, and `geojsonsf`, then run `quarto render`.

For other country results, edition details, and filters, head to [Country Explorer](explore.qmd).
